q: Three servers sit behind a round robin load balancer. Server B is slow and keeps each request open for 8 ticks, while A and C need 2. After 9 requests, B holds 3 open requests and A holds none. Why?
options: Round robin favors server B
Round robin counts turns, not work, so B keeps getting its turn while it is still busy
Server A was marked as dead
Round robin only sends requests to the slowest server
why: Round robin takes turns whatever each server is doing. Least connections looks at how many requests each server holds now, so in the same run it ends with 1 open request on each server.

q: A team uses least connections and has no health check. Server B crashes and refuses every request at once. What do users see?
options: Nothing, the load balancer skips B by itself
Half the users see errors
The load balancer slows down but still works
All requests go to B and fail, because a dead server shows 0 open connections and looks like the best one
why: B fails each request at once, so its count never grows, and the fewest connections always wins. A and C sit with spare room. A health check takes B out of the pool so the pick only looks at servers that are up.

q: A server crashes between two health checks. Can a user still see an error?
options: Yes. In the gap, the load balancer still sends B its turn. Retrying safe requests on another server hides it
No, a health check is instant
No, the user's browser skips dead servers
Yes, but only if the load balancer is also broken
why: A check is not instant. With the rule of 2 failed checks in a row, B stays in the pool until the second one fails, and a request that lands on B in that gap fails. It is nobody's bug.

q: You want requests to /images to go to file servers and requests to /orders to go to app servers. What kind of load balancer do you need?
options: Layer 4, because it is the fastest
Round robin, because it takes turns
Layer 7, because it reads the path and layer 4 does not
Any load balancer can do it
why: Layer 4 sees only the outside of the envelope: the address and the door number. Layer 7 opens it and reads the path, headers and cookie, so it can route by path. It is the default for a normal web app.

q: Every server's health route runs SELECT 1 on the shared database, and then the database goes down for everyone. What does the load balancer do?
options: Keeps all servers, because the servers are running fine
Removes all of them, so the whole site is down even though the servers are fine
Removes half of them to share the load
Switches to layer 4 automatically
why: Every server fails the check, so every server leaves the pool. A health check should show whether this server can do real work, but think about which shared things it should look at.

q: Every page waits on a slow database. Will a better load balancer help?
options: Yes, least connections fixes slow databases
Yes, add a second load balancer
Yes, switch from layer 4 to layer 7
No. All servers wait for the same database, so caching is the tool that helps
why: A load balancer shares requests between servers. It cannot make the one database behind them faster. It also cannot fix sticky sessions or jobs on a timer.
